results.title: Reggie Burrows Hodges prefers to disappear. Now his art and music are everywhere in L.A.
highlights:
[Reggie Burrows Hodges prefers to disappear. Now his art and music are everywhere in L.A.]

This week, three exhibitions opened across the city. At the Getty, “A Theater of Passions” riffs on compositions by the 17th century Baroque painters Orazio Gentileschi and his daughter Artemisia; at the California African American Museum, “A Theater of Miracles” imbues intimate encounters with the high drama of the Old Masters; and “A Theater of Dreams” draws on childhood memories, the city’s Black artistic legacy and Hodges’ travels in Europe.

Reggie Burrows Hodges, “Magic Eraser,” 2026, featured in “A Theater of Dreams” at Art + Practice.

Opening June 27 at our new home at 1 Beech Street in Lewiston, Maine MILL’s first special exhibition will be A Common Bond: The Brick Journal, guest curated by Alexis Iammarino @iammavision of Little Legs Projects @littlelegsprojects

Rooted in Lewiston-Auburn’s long history of brickmaking, the exhibition explores the stories, labor, materials, and memories embedded within the bricks that helped build the cities we know today. Through contemporary artistic interpretation and historical research, The Brick Journal invites visitors to look closer at the everyday materials that shape place, industry, and community.

results.title: The Dog House Gallery — Brooklyn Comedy Collective (BCC)
highlights:
[The Dog House Gallery — Brooklyn Comedy Collective (BCC) > CURRENT EXHIBITION > Elizabeth Saloka: “Bricks and Mortar”]

OPENING RECEPTION: Fri, October 9, 6-8pm

Exhibition Dates: Oct. 9, 2026 — Jan. 8, 2027

**Dog House Gallery is pleased to present Elizabeth Saloka: “Bricks and Mortar”** from Oct. 9, 2026 – Jan. 8, 2027. This selection of more than three dozen sidewalk snapshots documents Saloka’s earliest rock art against the backdrop of a pre-pandemic New York City. Alongside her early street photographs is a collection of more recently painted rocks. Together, the photographs and rock art give a peek into the progression of Saloka’s chosen subject matter and style over the span of a decade.

…

Her sculptures reproduce the visual language of everyday consumer culture—from candy bars and packaged foods to household products and nostalgic toys—while the irregularity of the stone beneath the image remains visible. The tension between recognizable commercial imagery and the imperfect, discarded material creates much of the work’s humor and appeal. Her practice also considers consumption, nostalgia, comfort, identity, and the ways ordinary objects accumulate personal meaning.

highlights:
[Climate-Responsive Bricks: Combining Ceramics and Architecture]

Rodriguez answered questions we had about the project which will be on view at the Tyler School of Art and Architecture’s main lobby from January 12 – February 7, 2026. Read more below.

…

George Rodriguez: This project started very organically. Both Laurin and I came in as new full-time faculty in the fall of 24. We each had to give a short presentation about our practice and quickly found common interest in navigating community spaces. The project started with a very simple question; how can we move to making structures that don’t rely so heavily on HVAC systems and the use of concrete as a building material. Bricks and clay blocks have been used in many parts of the world to passively cool spaces. We then wondered if there was a way to utilize bricks to prepare for changing climates be it more water or more heat. I came with material knowledge of clay and Laurin with an architectural design background.

Anthony Meier is pleased to present Be Like the Sun, Never Done, Rob Reynolds’ (b. 1966, Boston, MA; lives and works in Los Angeles, CA) third solo exhibition with the gallery, on view October 1–December 18, 2026. Bringing together several large-scale canvases alongside a suite of watercolors from the artist’s ongoing *New Suns* series, the exhibition considers atmosphere as subject, using light, color, and perception to explore the relationship between abstraction and representation, and between the visible world and the forces that shape it. At its core, the exhibition is a deeply personal reflection, rooted in sight and place and shaped by a lifetime of looking, from childhood to the present.

highlights:
[Relationalities: Conditions of Interdependence (2026) > Timetable > Friday, June 12]

- 6–6:15 pm: Welcome by Prof. Dr. Barbara Clausen, Juliane Bischoff (curator of Portikus) and Deiara Semeco Kouto (Städelschule program curator)
- 6:15–7 pm: Keynote: Hamza Walker (Director, The Brick, LA) – *Monuments* 
  This talk is about *MONUMENTS*, an exhibition featuring a selection of decommissioned monuments alongside works of contemporary art that address American history and national identity. Eight years in the making, this showcase marks the last several years of monument removals as an historic occasion. In presenting the monuments in dialogue with contemporary artworks, the exhibition aims to build a better understanding of our shared history and ideals while holding these markers of the past accountable to the present.
